index.subtitulo: Automation panel to configure, optimize and customize your Fedora Linux quickly and safely.
index.card_guiado_desc_1: By clicking Start, you get access to sessions that optimize, configure and make your Fedora installation more practical for everyday use.
index.card_guiado_desc_2: FAP is intuitive and explains every step clearly — but, by design, it does not back up your files. Although every command is tested, things can go wrong. So: read the tips carefully before applying any changes and, whenever possible, back up before moving forward.
index.footer_creditos: Fedora Advantage Panel — Made with ❤️ by VitãoTub

primeiros-passos.descricao: Before any configuration, update the system and enable essential repositories. These steps are prerequisite for all upcoming sessions.
primeiros-passos.atualizacao_desc: Updates the repository index, syncs security keys and downloads the latest versions of all system components.
primeiros-passos.aviso_reiniciar: 💡 It's recommended to restart your computer after applying system updates.
primeiros-passos.rpm_desc: Installs and syncs the official RPM Fusion repositories, adds AppStream metadata support and runs a security adjustment.
primeiros-passos.flatpak_desc: Adds the global Flathub repository and ensures the Flatpak package manager is installed on the system.
primeiros-passos.remover_fedora_flatpak_desc: Fedora ships with its own Flatpak repository, distinct from Flathub. Apps from it may be outdated compared to the official versions maintained by upstream developers — or, in some cases, may not even be the official packaging. Since you've already enabled Flathub above, this repository can be safely removed.
primeiros-passos.remover_fedora_flatpak_oque_faz:
ℹ️ What this command does, in order:
1. Removes Flatpak apps installed from the Fedora repository (and fedora-testing, if present)
2. ⚠️ Also deletes the saved data of those apps — settings, profiles, bookmarks, game saves. This is done by the --delete-data flag of flatpak uninstall, and is irreversible
3. Removes the fedora and fedora-testing repositories
4. Cleans orphaned runtimes left behind
primeiros-passos.remover_fedora_flatpak_aviso:
⚠️ Before you continue:
• This operation is irreversible — the data of removed apps goes away with them.
• Close all Flatpak apps that may be running (browsers, games, players).
• The Fedora Flatpak repository is independent from Fedora's RPM repositories. Removing it does not affect dnf, security updates, or system packages.
primeiros-passos.remover_fedora_flatpak_confirm1:
⚠️ You are about to remove the Fedora Flatpak repository.

This will:
• Remove Flatpak apps installed from the Fedora repository
• DELETE the data of those apps (settings, profiles, bookmarks, saves) — irreversible
• Remove the fedora and fedora-testing repositories
• Clean up orphaned runtimes

Close all running Flatpak apps before continuing.

Continue?
primeiros-passos.remover_fedora_flatpak_confirm2:
🔄 Final confirmation!

The data of the Fedora repository Flatpak apps will be PERMANENTLY lost.

Are you absolutely sure?

codecs.descricao: This session brings together everything Fedora needs to handle content that isn't in the official repositories: media codecs (to play videos and audio in any format), commercial DVD playback, and Windows fonts (for compatibility with documents and programs that depend on them).
codecs.codecs_desc: Replaces ffmpeg-free with the full unrestricted version, installs essential gstreamer plugins and enables Cisco OpenH264.
codecs.codecs_info: ℹ️ What this solves: videos in MP4, MKV, AVI, WebM and other formats play in any player (VLC, MPV, Firefox, Chromium). Without these codecs, many files simply won't open or will play without audio/video. It's also a prerequisite for video editing in tools like Kdenlive and Shotcut.
codecs.extras_titulo: Commercial DVD Playback and Additional Firmware
codecs.extras_desc: Enables the restricted sub-repositories (tainted) that bring the libdvdcss library for reading commercial DVDs and proprietary firmware for some hardware.
codecs.extras_info: ℹ️ What this solves: without libdvdcss, Fedora can't read commercial DVDs (with CSS protection) — only homemade DVDs or video files. This item also enables proprietary firmware for some devices that lack a free driver.
codecs.fontes_desc: Installs the Microsoft fonts installer from SourceForge to get Arial, Times, Calibri, etc.
codecs.fontes_aviso: ⚠️ This process downloads and installs proprietary Microsoft fonts. Make sure you comply with the licensing terms.
codecs.fontes_info: ℹ️ Fonts installed: Arial, Times New Roman, Calibri, Cambria, Candara, Consolas, Constantia, Corbel, and others. What this solves: documents in LibreOffice, OnlyOffice and other programs look correct — without these fonts, the system substitutes alternatives that may break the formatting.

hardware.descricao: Hardware-specific settings. Choose your GPU type (AMD, NVIDIA or Intel) below to see the corresponding drivers and tools. For controllers, webcams, Wi-Fi and other peripherals, use the Devices and Peripherals session.
hardware.vulkan_desc: Installs the Vulkan libraries (32-bit and 64-bit), Mesa 3D with the RADV driver (AMD's open-source Vulkan driver), diagnostic tools and compatibility drivers. Essential for Steam, Proton and native games.
hardware.vaapi_desc: Hardware video acceleration drivers for smooth playback and encoding. RPM Fusion (Session 1) is a prerequisite for the freeworld version.
hardware.vaapi_aviso: 💡 Both buttons install VA-API drivers. The first uses Fedora's default driver; the second applies mesa-va-drivers-freeworld, an alternative for AMD GPUs that don't work with the default. If you're unsure, use the first one.
hardware.corectrl_desc: GUI for fan, clock and voltage control on AMD GPUs.
hardware.lact_desc: Modern alternative to CoreCtrl for fan, clock and voltage control on AMD GPUs.
hardware.overclock_desc: Enables the amdgpu.ppfeaturemask kernel parameter, unlocking advanced clock and voltage adjustments in CoreCtrl and LACT.
hardware.overclock_aviso: ⚠️ Requires reboot. Only enable if you know what you're doing — bad overclock can cause instability.
hardware.nvidia_aviso: ⚠️ Without nvidia-drm.modeset=1, Wayland is unstable with NVIDIA cards. RPM Fusion (Session 1) is a prerequisite for proprietary drivers. After installing anything here, reboot your computer.
hardware.nvidia_driver_desc: Detects your NVIDIA GPU generation and automatically installs the correct driver series — akmod-nvidia for Turing and newer, akmod-nvidia-580xx for Maxwell/Pascal, akmod-nvidia-470xx for Kepler and akmod-nvidia-390xx for Fermi. Includes the CUDA + NVENC/NVDEC library extras for OBS, Kdenlive and hardware encoding.
hardware.nvidia_driver_info: ℹ️ About detection: FAP reads the GPU model via lspci and chooses the correct package. Installing the wrong series (e.g., akmod-nvidia on a GTX 750 Ti) results in a black screen after reboot — this detection prevents that. If no NVIDIA GPU is found, the command aborts with a clear message and nothing is installed.
hardware.nvidia_confirmar_reverter:
⚠️ Revert the NVIDIA driver?

The system will go back to using the nouveau driver (open-source, included in Fedora by default).

Gaming and 3D application performance will be reduced until you reinstall the proprietary driver.

Continue?
hardware.nvidia_sem_gpu: No NVIDIA GPU was detected on this system. The proprietary driver only applies to physical NVIDIA GPUs.
hardware.nvidia_sem_rpmfusion: RPM Fusion Nonfree is not active. Enable it in the First Steps session before installing the driver.
hardware.nvidia_panel_sem_gpu_desc: This system doesn't have a physical NVIDIA GPU, so the proprietary driver doesn't apply here. The Install NVIDIA Driver button is disabled.
hardware.nvidia_panel_instalado_sem_gpu: Since the driver is marked as installed but no NVIDIA GPU was detected, use the Revert to nouveau button below to clean the system.
hardware.nvidia_panel_rpmfusion_aviso: ⚠️ RPM Fusion Nonfree is not active. Enable it in the First Steps session before installing the driver.
hardware.nvidia_modeset_desc: Enables the nvidia-drm.modeset=1 kernel parameter, required for Wayland to work correctly with NVIDIA cards.
hardware.intel_aviso: ⚠️ These packages are for Intel iGPUs (integrated graphics). If you have a dedicated AMD or NVIDIA GPU, the dedicated card's driver handles most acceleration — the Intel drivers may still be useful if you use the iGPU in tandem, but they're not mandatory.
hardware.intel_media_desc: The intel-media-driver package enables hardware video acceleration on Intel iGPUs Skylake (6th generation) or newer. It reduces CPU usage when watching 4K videos, using the browser and editing video. Older chips (Haswell or earlier) use the i965 driver, which already ships with Fedora.

dispositivos-perifericos.descricao: Detects hardware that may need additional drivers or firmware (not included in Fedora for licensing reasons), offers safe supplements, and lets you enable community repositories for specific devices. Nothing is installed automatically — each suggestion has separate install and revert buttons.
dispositivos-perifericos.deteccao_desc: Click the button below to scan your computer. FAP will identify GPUs, network cards and USB adapters that may need additional drivers, cross-referencing hardware IDs against a community-maintained map. Nothing is installed automatically — each suggestion appears as a separate card, with explicit install and revert buttons.
dispositivos-perifericos.suplementos_desc: These packages complement Fedora's standard linux-firmware. They are safe to install on any system — they don't conflict with existing drivers and cover hardware that Red Hat doesn't distribute for licensing reasons or because it's outside Fedora's scope.
dispositivos-perifericos.firmware_vendor_desc: The linux-firmware-vendor package brings firmware that isn't in the main package — recent Realtek Wi-Fi chips (RTL8852), some Intel models, and vendor firmware that requires restricted redistribution. It complements linux-firmware, it doesn't replace it.
dispositivos-perifericos.copr_aviso:
⚠️ Attention before continuing:
• These repositories are maintained by third parties (individuals or small community groups), not by Red Hat or RPM Fusion.
• FAP does not control the content, update frequency or security of the packages.
• A COPR can be discontinued at any time — if that happens, the driver stops receiving updates until someone publishes an alternative.
• Only install if you have one of the listed devices.
• If you don't know whether you need it, use the automatic detection in the accordion above first — it identifies the exact model.
dispositivos-perifericos.copr_openrazer_desc: RGB and macros for Razer mice, keyboards and laptops. Uses the official OpenRazer repository and the Polychromatic frontend. Adds your user to the plugdev group — requires logout/login.
dispositivos-perifericos.copr_xpadneo_desc: The xpadneo driver for Xbox One/Series controllers via Bluetooth and the wireless dongle. Enables force feedback, audio and battery reading. Requires reboot after installation.
dispositivos-perifericos.broadcom_desc: Proprietary akmod-wl driver for Broadcom Wi-Fi chips (common in old laptops and MacBooks). Lives in RPM Fusion Nonfree — which is already enabled in Session 1 (First Steps). Only install if the open-source driver (brcmfmac/b43) doesn't work.
dispositivos-perifericos.confirmar_reverter_tudo:
⚠️ Attention!

You are about to fully revert this item:

• The package will be uninstalled
• The repository will be removed
• Group changes (if any) will be undone

If you depend on this driver (for example, a Wi-Fi adapter or controller), you'll lose functionality.

Continue?
dispositivos-perifericos.input_add_desc: Required for Steam Input, xpadneo and controller drivers to recognize the user. Works for Xbox, PlayStation and Nintendo controllers using kernel drivers.
dispositivos-perifericos.input_add_aviso: ℹ️ Requires logout/login to take effect.
dispositivos-perifericos.steam_devices_desc: Installs the udev rules from the steam-devices package, which allow the system to correctly recognize Xbox, PlayStation and Nintendo controllers when used with Steam.
dispositivos-perifericos.steam_devices_info: ℹ️ What this solves: without these rules, some controllers may not be detected by Steam even when connected. It's a small package that complements the input group above — the group gives your user permission, and this package teaches the system to identify each controller model.
dispositivos-perifericos.aviso_rpmfusion_corpo: Some drivers (NVIDIA, Broadcom, Realtek Ethernet) require RPM Fusion. Enable it in the First Steps session before installing these drivers.
dispositivos-perifericos.aviso_secureboot_corpo: To use the NVIDIA driver, you need to register the MOK key during installation or disable Secure Boot. Without that, the driver won't load and the machine may boot in minimal resolution.
dispositivos-perifericos.sem_dispositivos: No device with an additional driver suggestion was detected. Your hardware works with Fedora's default drivers.
dispositivos-perifericos.ja_funciona: This device already works with the standard driver ({driver}). We don't recommend installing the proprietary driver — it can cause conflicts.
dispositivos-perifericos.ja_instalado: The suggested driver is already installed on this system.
dispositivos-perifericos.precisa_driver: This device may need the {pkg} package. Install it if the hardware isn't working correctly.
dispositivos-perifericos.copr_necessario: This driver lives in the community repository {copr}. Enable the repository in the "Community drivers" accordion before installing.

notes.nvidia: Requires RPM Fusion nonfree. FAP tries to use nvidia-detect to identify the exact generation and suggest the correct package (akmod-nvidia, akmod-nvidia-470xx or akmod-nvidia-390xx).
notes.amd_gpu: Hardware video acceleration (VA-API) on AMD GPUs. Fedora's default Mesa blocks this support due to licensing.
notes.amd_apu: AMD APUs with integrated graphics (Ryzen with Radeon Vega or RDNA).
notes.intel_gpu: Video acceleration on Intel iGPUs Skylake (6th gen) or newer. Older chips (Haswell or earlier) use the i965 driver, already in Fedora.
notes.broadcom_wifi: Only install if the open-source driver (brcmfmac/b43) doesn't work. akmod-wl conflicts with them and can take down a working Wi-Fi.
notes.realtek_ethernet: Alternative driver for Realtek Ethernet cards. The default driver (r8169) works in most cases — only install akmod-r8168 if the cable isn't recognized.

dispositivos-perifericos.confirmar_reverter:
⚠️ Attention!

You are about to revert a driver.

If the device depends on this driver to work (for example, a Wi-Fi adapter), you will lose functionality after reboot.

Have an alternative connection available before continuing.

Continue?

producao-multimidia.descricao: Tools to record, edit, stream and produce audio and video content on Fedora.
producao-multimidia.obs_titulo: 🎬 OBS Studio - Installation and Virtual Camera
producao-multimidia.obs_desc: Install OBS Studio for recording/streaming and enable the virtual camera for video calls.
producao-multimidia.obs_aviso: ⚠️ The virtual camera requires Secure Boot to be configured correctly or disabled.
producao-multimidia.easyeffects_desc: Sound effects processor for PipeWire to apply noise reduction and equalization.

aplicativos.bloco1_desc: Tools to work with documents, notes, email and e-books.
aplicativos.bloco2_desc: Video, music and streaming players to consume content day to day.
aplicativos.bloco3_desc: Image editing, vector illustration, 3D modeling, CAD and 3D printing.
aplicativos.bloco4_desc: Browsers, video call apps and messengers.
aplicativos.bloco5_desc: Video editors, 3D modeling, audio editing and music production.
aplicativos.bloco6_desc: Tools to sync files with Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox and other services.
aplicativos.affinity_desc: Affinity has no native Linux version. This button opens the AffinityOnLinux installer, a community project (not affiliated with Serif/Canva) that sets up a pre-configured Wine environment to run Affinity.
aplicativos.affinity_aviso: ⚠️ You must have purchased and downloaded the Affinity .exe installer from the official Serif/Canva website before using this — FAP only prepares the Wine environment and opens the community installer; that installer will ask for the .exe file at the right moment. It's a third-party project: if something doesn't work on your hardware, check their known issues page.
aplicativos.affinity_prereq: 📦 Prerequisite: PyQt6 is required for the installer interface. FAP checks and installs it automatically if needed.
aplicativos.lightworks_aviso: ⚠️ Note: Lightworks is not installed via Flatpak. The button downloads the RPM package directly from the official LWKS website. Updates are not automatic — to update, run this button again.
aplicativos.rclone_aviso: ℹ️ Cloud account setup: Rclone Manager is a graphical interface for Rclone. It lets you configure access to Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, S3, and dozens of other cloud storage services. After installing both apps, open Rclone Manager and follow the guide inside its interface to add your accounts. FAP only installs the tools — setting up the accounts is done by you, inside Rclone Manager.

casa-escritorio.descricao: Settings to get Fedora ready for home and office use: printer, file sharing with Windows/phone, password manager and PDF reading with OCR. All in independent blocks — use only what you need.
casa-escritorio.cups_desc: Installs Fedora's printing system (CUPS), support for automatic network printer discovery (Avahi/Bonjour) and generic drivers. After installing, most modern printers are recognized automatically in Settings → Printers.
casa-escritorio.cups_info: ℹ️ What is installed: cups, avahi (network discovery), system-config-printer (management GUI) and ghostscript (format conversion). The CUPS service is enabled automatically.
casa-escritorio.cups_info_drivers: ℹ️ About specific drivers: HP printers may need hplip, Brother needs brother-* (from the manufacturer's site), Epson needs epson-inkjet-printer-escpr. After installing CUPS, open Printer Settings — the system suggests the missing drivers.
casa-escritorio.compart_desc: Tools to transfer and share files between Fedora and other devices. Choose according to your case: Windows on the local network (Samba), Android/iPhone (LocalSend) or Linux network (Warpinator).
casa-escritorio.samba_desc: Installs Samba, which allows sharing Fedora folders with Windows computers on the same network — and also accessing Windows shared folders from Fedora.
casa-escritorio.samba_aviso: ⚠️ After installing: open Nautilus/Dolphin, right-click a folder → Properties → Sharing (or Folder Sharing) and check "Share this folder". Fedora takes care of the rest.
casa-escritorio.samba_info: ℹ️ What is installed: samba, samba-client and cifs-utils (to mount Windows folders). The smb and nmb services are enabled.
casa-escritorio.localsend_desc: Cross-platform app (Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS) that sends files between devices on the same local network. It's the modern alternative to AirDrop — works across any combination of systems, with a simple interface.
casa-escritorio.localsend_info: ℹ️ How to use: install LocalSend on Fedora (via FAP) and on your phone (via app store). Open both on the same Wi-Fi network, and the devices find each other automatically. No account, no cloud, no ads.
casa-escritorio.warpinator_desc: File transfer tool from Linux Mint, available for Fedora. Simple and direct: open it, it finds other Warpinator devices on the network and transfers files with one click. Ideal if you have more than one Linux at home.
casa-escritorio.warpinator_info: ℹ️ When to use: if the destination is also Linux, Warpinator is often faster than LocalSend (less overhead). For phone, use LocalSend.
casa-escritorio.keepassxc_desc: Local, open-source, cloud-free password manager. Stores everything in an encrypted .kdbx file on your computer — you decide if you sync it (via Nextcloud, Syncthing, USB drive, etc). Integrates with browsers and supports autofill.
casa-escritorio.keepassxc_info: ℹ️ Why KeePassXC instead of Bitwarden? KeePassXC is 100% offline and local — nothing leaves your computer. Ideal for those who prefer not to depend on any service. If you prefer cloud convenience, Bitwarden is also a good option (but FAP installs KeePassXC, which is more aligned with the local-first philosophy).
casa-escritorio.okular_tesseract_titulo: Okular + Tesseract — PDF Reader with OCR
casa-escritorio.okular_tesseract_desc: Installs Okular (PDF, e-book and comic reader, very fast) and Tesseract (OCR engine). With both, you can open a scanned PDF (image) and extract the text — useful for copying excerpts from scanned documents.
casa-escritorio.okular_tesseract_info: ℹ️ What is OCR: Optical Character Recognition — converts text images (scanned, photographed) into searchable and copyable text. Tesseract supports Portuguese, English and 100+ languages. In Okular, use Tools → Text Selection on scanned PDFs (with Tesseract installed, it recognizes automatically).
casa-escritorio.okular_tesseract_info_lang: ℹ️ Additional OCR languages: we install the base package with Portuguese and English. If you need another language, look for tesseract-langpack-XX in Discover/GNOME Software.

gaming.descricao: Installs the main launchers, Windows compatibility tools (Wine/Proton), performance and monitoring utilities, and provides ready-to-use tips to optimize the gaming experience on Fedora.
gaming.launchers_desc: Install the main game launchers for Fedora.
gaming.launchers_info: ℹ️ All launchers are installed via Flatpak.
gaming.compat_desc: Tools to run Windows games and programs outside of Steam, and resources that help with compatibility.
gaming.compat_info_extra: ℹ️ Winetricks installs extra components (fonts, libraries) inside a Wine prefix. Bottles is a modern alternative to plain Wine, with visual management of "bottles" (prefixes) and support for Proton-GE runners. NTSYNC is a kernel module that brings significant performance and compatibility improvements for Windows games via Wine/Proton.
gaming.ntsync_aviso: ⚠️ What is NTSYNC? It's a Linux kernel module that implements Windows thread synchronization natively in the kernel, reducing CPU overhead and improving game smoothness (fewer micro-stutters and more stable frame times). It's safe to enable — Fedora 44 already enables it by default for Wine/Steam. Recommended for GE-Proton users, where NTSYNC support is already native. The default Wine from repositories does not benefit from NTSYNC yet — in that case, the real gain comes when running games via Proton/GE-Proton. The module will be loaded automatically and will persist between reboots. If a game still doesn't recognize it, restart your computer.
gaming.performance_desc: Tools that optimize performance during gameplay and allow monitoring FPS, CPU/GPU usage and other metrics.
gaming.performance_info_extra: ℹ️ GameMode sets CPU/GPU to maximum priority while a game is running. MangoHud shows an FPS/CPU/GPU overlay inside the game. Goverlay is a graphical interface to configure MangoHud without editing text files. Gamescope is a Valve micro-compositor that enables upscaling (FSR/NIS), FPS limiting, HDR and more.
gaming.gamescope_nvidia_flatpak_aviso: ⚠️ Gamescope + NVIDIA + Flatpak — attention: Gamescope was designed by Valve for the Mesa architecture (AMD/Intel). On NVIDIA cards with the proprietary driver, it can present instability — black screen, frozen cursor or the game closing on open. Additionally, native Gamescope (installed via dnf) has difficulty interacting with games that run inside the Flatpak sandbox, and vice versa. Recommendation: keep everything in the same format. If you use Steam/Heroic via Flatpak, prefer also installing the Flatpak Gamescope extensions; if you use native Steam, prefer native Gamescope. On NVIDIA GPUs, if Gamescope doesn't work well, consider using MangoHud + GameMode as an alternative — they don't have this limitation.
gaming.avancado_desc: Tools for those who want to get the most out of Fedora for gaming: specific Proton versions, image post-processing, performance presets and a dedicated gamescope session.
gaming.protonup_desc: Graphical interface that downloads and manages Proton-GE versions (community version of Proton, with extra fixes), plus runners for Lutris and Bottles.
gaming.protonup_info: ℹ️ After installing, open ProtonUp-Qt, choose the recommended Proton-GE version and click "Download". The latest version usually works well for most games.
gaming.vkbasalt_desc: Post-processing layer that adds sharpening, vibrance, FXAA, SMAA and other visual effects directly to Vulkan output. Useful for games that look a bit blurry by default.
gaming.vkbasalt_aviso: ⚠️ How to use: after installing, each game needs to enable vkBasalt individually. On Steam, add ENABLE_VKBASALT=1 %command% to the game's launch options. Outside Steam, set the ENABLE_VKBASALT=1 variable before running.
gaming.gamemode_presets_desc: Creates ready-to-use config files for MangoHud (FPS overlay) and GameMode (CPU/GPU priority). You get a clean, readable overlay without configuring anything manually.
gaming.gamemode_presets_info: ℹ️ Files are created at ~/.config/MangoHud/MangoHud.conf and ~/.config/gamemode.ini. If you already have custom files, they'll be overwritten — back them up beforehand if needed.
gaming.gamescope_session_titulo: Gamescope Session — Gaming mode on boot
gaming.gamescope_session_desc: Installs an alternative login session that boots the computer directly into Gamescope (the same mode Steam Deck uses). Ideal for HTPCs and TV-connected machines.
gaming.gamescope_session_aviso: ⚠️ Note: this is an alternative session — it appears on your display manager's login screen (GDM, SDDM, etc). Your normal session (KDE/GNOME) stays intact. You choose which one to enter at each boot.
gaming.controller_test_desc: Installs a graphical tool to test buttons, analog stick dead zones, trigger response and controller rumble. Useful for diagnosing controllers with drift or buttons that don't respond.
gaming.emuladores_desc: Emulators for classic and modern consoles on Fedora. All available via Flatpak.
gaming.emuladores_aviso_geral: ⚠️ Important notice: some emulators require BIOS, firmware or system files dumped from the original console to work. FAP does not provide these files for legal reasons. Consult each emulator's official documentation for how to obtain them from your own console.
gaming.retroarch_desc: Universal emulation frontend that runs dozens of consoles via "cores" (plugins). A single app for SNES, Mega Drive, NES, Game Boy, GBA, PS1 and many others.
gaming.retroarch_info: ℹ️ How to install cores: after opening RetroArch, use the Online Updater → Core Downloader menu to download the cores you want (snes9x, genesis_plus_gx, nestopia, mgba, beetle_psx, mupen64plus_next, etc).
gaming.dolphin_desc: Mature and very compatible emulator for GameCube and Wii. Runs most games at higher resolution than the original, with upscaling.
gaming.pcsx2_desc: PlayStation 2 emulator with upscaling support, widescreen patches and high compatibility with the console's catalog.
gaming.pcsx2_aviso: ⚠️ Requires PlayStation 2 BIOS. The BIOS must be dumped from your own console. FAP does not provide this file. After installing, consult the PCSX2 documentation for where to place the BIOS.
gaming.rpcs3_desc: PlayStation 3 emulator under active development. Compatibility varies per game — some run perfectly, others still have issues. Check the official compatibility list before installing.
gaming.rpcs3_aviso: ⚠️ Requires PlayStation 3 firmware. The firmware must be downloaded from Sony's official website (Sony provides firmware publicly for console updates) and installed by RPCS3 itself. FAP does not download or install this file.
gaming.rpcs3_info_extra: ℹ️ About the "unofficial build" notice: RPCS3 may show a message on first run indicating it was installed from an unofficial package. This is a warning from the emulator itself — the Flathub Flatpak is the official distribution channel for RPCS3 on Linux, and the warning does not affect functionality.
gaming.duckstation_desc: Modern and lightweight PlayStation 1 emulator, with high resolution support, graphical filters and support for modern controllers. A more user-friendly alternative to the classic ePSXe.
gaming.duckstation_aviso: ⚠️ May require PlayStation 1 BIOS. Although Duckstation has a built-in HLE BIOS (works without BIOS for many games), some titles require the real BIOS to function correctly. The BIOS must be dumped from your own console.
gaming.anticheat_desc: Informational panel about which anti-cheats work on Linux, which don't, and why. Nothing here is installed or executed — it's just for you to know before buying or trying a game.
gaming.dicas_desc: Recommended settings to get the most out of games on Fedora.
gaming.dicas_aviso_steam: 💡 Steam — Launch Options: you can add commands to each game's launch options (right-click the game → Properties → Launch Options). Examples:
gaming.dicas_nota: ℹ️ Replace the -W and -H values with the desired resolution. -r 60 limits FPS to 60 — remove it if you want unlimited FPS.

waydroid.aviso_nvidia: ⚠️ Waydroid requires AMD or Intel GPU. Users with NVIDIA GPU cannot use this session (the proprietary driver doesn't expose the required Mesa). There's an experimental project (waydroid-nvidia) that tries to work around it via Vulkan proxy, but it's not supported by FAP.
waydroid.descricao: Waydroid runs Android inside a container on Fedora. This session installs Waydroid, initializes the container with the Android image, and offers the most requested extras (Google Play Store, ARM translation, Magisk, Widevine).
waydroid.waydroid_desc: Installs Waydroid and lzip (dependency for the extras script). We use the COPR yanqiyu/waydroid because the official package is broken on Fedora 44 (Bug 2420131) and the COPR has the working version for Fedora 44/45.
waydroid.init_desc: Downloads the Android images (system ~1.2 GB + vendor ~190 MB) and initializes the container. Uses the GAPPS variant (with Google Apps). Runs once — after that, use "Open Waydroid" to start the container whenever you want.
waydroid.open_desc: Opens the Android interface. Starts the container if it's not running. The container must be running to install extras (GApps, Magisk, etc.). Click here once before using the extras.
waydroid.uninstall_desc: Removes absolutely everything this session installs: the Waydroid package, the Android container (images, apps, data), the extras repository (~/.local/share/FAP-waydroid), the Python venv, and the menu shortcut created by Waydroid. Irreversible action.
waydroid.confirmar_uninstall: This will remove Waydroid and ALL Android container data (installed apps, settings). Continue?
waydroid.prep_desc: Clones waydroid_script, creates an isolated Python environment (venv) and installs dependencies. This step is a prerequisite for all extras below. Runs once.
waydroid.prep_aviso: ⚠️ Requires Waydroid to be installed, initialized AND with the container running (use "Open Waydroid" above). Without that, the extras fail.
waydroid.gapps_desc: Installs Google apps, including the Google Play Store, in the Android container. Requires the Extras Environment to be prepared and the container running.
waydroid.arm_desc: Allows running Android apps compiled for ARM on x86_64 machines. libndk usually has better performance on AMD CPUs; libhoudini is the traditional option for Intel. Install only one of them.
waydroid.magisk_desc: Advanced suite for Android users. Provides root and module management inside the container. Requires the Extras Environment to be prepared.
waydroid.widevine_desc: DRM L3 support for services like Netflix, Spotify and other streaming inside the Android container. Requires the Extras Environment to be prepared.
waydroid.smartdock_desc: Support for Logitech SmartDock hardware. Requires the Extras Environment to be prepared.
waydroid.helper_desc: GUI for advanced Waydroid configuration. Installation via the official COPR cuteneko/waydroid-helper.
waydroid.prefs_desc: Applies tweaks that improve usability (independent windows, proper DPI, touch behavior in games).
waydroid.prefs_aviso: ⚠️ The Waydroid container must be running for these settings to apply. Open Waydroid once before using this button.
waydroid.container_running: Waydroid container is running. You can install the extras.
waydroid.container_stopped: Waydroid container is not running. Click "Open Waydroid" in the section above before using the extras.
waydroid.container_not_ready: Waydroid is not installed or initialized yet. Follow the steps in the section above first.
waydroid.container_waiting: Waiting for the container to come up (up to 3 minutes)...
waydroid.container_timeout: Container did not respond within 3 minutes. Check /tmp/FAP-waydroid-ui.log for details.
waydroid.container_guard_alert: Waydroid container is not running. Click "Open Waydroid" first.

virtualizacao.descricao: Tools to run virtual machines on Fedora. Each option targets a different user profile — QEMU/KVM is the native stack (most performant), VirtualBox offers a familiar interface for those coming from Windows, and GNOME Boxes simplifies the experience for beginners.
virtualizacao.confirmar_remover:
⚠️ Are you sure you want to remove {nome}?

Virtual machines you created will NOT be deleted — only the software will be removed from the system.
virtualizacao.qemu_desc: Native Linux virtualization stack. Runs virtual machines with hardware acceleration via KVM — it's the most performant option and the base for all other solutions. Installs QEMU, the libvirt daemon, virt-manager (graphical interface) and enables the system service.
virtualizacao.qemu_info: ℹ️ About permissions: your user is added to the libvirt group so you can manage VMs without a password on every action. The group only takes effect after logout/login — until then, virt-manager will ask for the administrator password when opening.
virtualizacao.virtualbox_desc: Oracle's cross-platform virtualization software. Good choice for those already familiar with VirtualBox on other platforms. Requires RPM Fusion (Session 1) for the akmod-VirtualBox kernel module, which automatically rebuilds on each new kernel.
virtualizacao.virtualbox_info: ℹ️ QEMU/KVM vs VirtualBox: both run virtual machines, but QEMU/KVM is more performant on Linux (native kernel integration). VirtualBox is preferable when you already have virtual disks in .vdi format or depend on its specific features.
virtualizacao.boxes_desc: Simplified graphical interface to create and manage virtual machines. Uses QEMU/KVM under the hood, so it's as performant as virt-manager — the difference is the experience: instead of configuring CPU, RAM and disk separately, you point to an .iso file and it handles the rest.
virtualizacao.boxes_info: ℹ️ Recommended for: those starting with virtualization and wanting to test a Linux distribution or Windows without manually configuring anything. If you're already experienced, prefer virt-manager — it offers more control over the VM.

diagnostico.descricao: Visual panel of system state. Shows in real time what's happening with CPU, memory, disk and services — without needing to open the terminal. Useful for investigating slowness, disk usage, temperature and recent errors.
diagnostico.aviso_geral: ℹ️ This panel is read-only. No command here changes the system — they're all queries. If you want to fix something specific, the actions are in the other FAP sessions.
diagnostico.painel_desc: Data collected from FAP's local endpoints. Some values update automatically; others can be updated manually.
diagnostico.top5_desc: Processes consuming the most CPU and memory right now.
diagnostico.otimizacoes_desc: Shows the current state of the performance tunings that can be applied in the Tunings and Maintenance session. Values in green indicate the tuning is active; neutral values indicate Fedora's default. This section is informational only — to apply or revert a tuning, use the buttons in the corresponding session.
diagnostico.otimizacoes_info: ℹ️ About the values: this section only shows what's currently active. Each tuning is reversible and can be applied or reverted individually in the Tunings and Maintenance session. If a tuning is blank or shows "N/A", the feature may not be available on this kernel — it's not an error.
diagnostico.armazen_desc: See how much space each partition is using. Useful when the system warns "disk full" or when you don't know what's eating up space.
diagnostico.particoes_desc: Lists mounted partitions with usage, free space and mount point.
diagnostico.saude_desc: Disk health check (HDDs and SSDs) via SMART and reading component temperatures (CPU, GPU, motherboard). Helps detect problems before they become serious failure.
diagnostico.gsmart_desc: Installs GSmartControl, a graphical interface for smartctl. It shows disk health, temperature, hours of use, bad sectors, and allows running quick and extended tests with a click.
diagnostico.gsmart_info: ℹ️ How to interpret: in the "Health" column, a green ✅ means a healthy disk. A red ❌ means failure — back up immediately. Temperatures above 55°C under continuous use deserve attention.
diagnostico.gsmart_info_root: ℹ️ About the password: when opening GSmartControl, it may ask for administrator password to read SMART data — this is normal (the smartctl needs access to the physical device). The password window comes from the system, not from FAP.
diagnostico.coolercontrol_desc: Installs CoolerControl, a complete monitoring and thermal control center. In addition to showing temperatures, fan speeds and other sensors in real time, it lets you create custom fan curves (for example, "when the GPU reaches 60°C, spin the fan at 50%"). It's the most robust and official thermal management tool on Fedora.
diagnostico.coolercontrol_info:
ℹ️ What you can do with it:
  • View temperatures of CPU, GPU and motherboard in real time
  • View speed (RPM) of all system fans
  • Create custom fan curves based on any sensor
  • Configure alerts for high temperatures or fan failures
  • Build dashboards with the data you use the most
diagnostico.coolercontrol_info_copr: ℹ️ About installation: CoolerControl is not in Fedora's standard repositories. We use the project's official COPR (codifryed/CoolerControl), maintained by the developer himself.
diagnostico.coolercontrol_info_group: ℹ️ About permissions: FAP adds your user to the coolercontrol group so the GUI can control fans without asking for a password on every action. That group only takes effect after logging out and back in. The daemon starts working immediately.
diagnostico.coolercontrol_info_sensors: ℹ️ If a sensor doesn't appear: CoolerControl uses the same sensors as lm_sensors. If a sensor is missing, open the terminal and run sudo sensors-detect, answering "YES" to all questions. Then restart the service: sudo systemctl restart coolercontrold.
diagnostico.journal_desc: Filters the systemd journal for error messages from the last 24 hours and groups them by origin — so you quickly see if something is failing repeatedly without having to read the raw log.
diagnostico.journal_info: ℹ️ Important: not every error in the journal is a problem. Services that try to start before the hardware is ready, or drivers that report warnings during boot, are normal. Use this panel to detect patterns: the same error appearing dozens of times indicates something that needs attention.

ajustes-manutencao.descricao: Optional performance and audio tunings, basic system settings (locale, DNF, dual-boot) and periodic Fedora maintenance tools.
ajustes-manutencao.tuning_desc: Recommended adjustments to improve system responsiveness in games and general use. Each item is independent and can be reverted at any time.
ajustes-manutencao.vm_max_map_count_titulo: Memory Adjustments for Games and Heavy Applications
ajustes-manutencao.vm_max_map_count_desc: Increases the maximum number of memory areas each process can map. Fedora's default is 65530, insufficient for modern games — several titles fail to launch or crash due to lack of mappable memory (Hogwarts Legacy, Counter-Strike 2, The Finals, Star Citizen, among others).
ajustes-manutencao.vm_max_map_count_info: ℹ️ What changes: the limit goes from 65,530 to 2,147,483,642 (the practical maximum). It's a compatibility fix, not a "tweak".
ajustes-manutencao.vm_swappiness_cache_desc: Adjusts two kernel parameters that control swap and file cache. Fedora ships with conservative values; these adjustments make the system keep more RAM available for foreground applications and retain disk caches longer.
ajustes-manutencao.tcp_bbr_desc: Replaces the default TCP congestion control algorithm (cubic) with BBR, developed by Google. It improves latency and throughput on connections with packet loss — benefits online gaming, streaming and downloads.
ajustes-manutencao.audio_tuning_desc: Adjustments that improve the experience for those who record, produce or game with real-time audio. Recommended for users of Ardour, LMMS, Reaper or those who stream with live monitoring.
ajustes-manutencao.realtime_setup_desc: Configures the system to allow audio applications to have real-time priority. Without this, audio may present glitches (crackling or xruns) under load.
ajustes-manutencao.realtime_setup_info:
ℹ️ What changes:
• realtime group created with adequate memory limits.
• Your user added to this group — requires logout/login.
• Configuration files installed by the official realtime-setup package.
ajustes-manutencao.realtime_setup_aviso: ⚠️ Requires logout/login: the realtime group only takes effect after you log out and back in.
ajustes-manutencao.pipewire_quantum_desc: Reduces the PipeWire quantum (audio buffer size) from 1024 to 256 samples. Reduces audio latency from ~21ms to ~5ms — essential for recording and games with positional audio.
ajustes-manutencao.pipewire_quantum_info:
ℹ️ What changes:
• Creates ~/.config/pipewire/pipewire.conf.d/99-FAP-quantum.conf.
• Restarts pipewire, pipewire-pulse and wireplumber.
• Applies immediately — no reboot.
• Trade-off: lower latency uses slightly more CPU. On modest machines, it can cause crackling.
ajustes-manutencao.dnf_desc: Configures simultaneous parallel downloads and enables automatic lookup of the fastest server mirror.
ajustes-manutencao.dnf_info_extra: ℹ️ The setting will be applied with the selected value. You can reapply with different values at any time.
ajustes-manutencao.idioma_desc: Install translation packages, spell checker, and change the system default locale.
ajustes-manutencao.idioma_aviso: ⚠️ Note: Restart your computer after completing step 3 to apply the language changes!
ajustes-manutencao.dual_boot_desc: Makes Fedora use the hardware clock in local time (the same way Windows does by default), fixing the wrong time when switching between systems.
ajustes-manutencao.dual_boot_aviso: 💡 By default, Windows stores the hardware clock in local time, while Linux (Fedora) stores it in UTC. This button configures Fedora to use local time, matching Windows' behavior — so you don't need to change anything on Windows.
ajustes-manutencao.dual_boot_confirmar:
⚠️ Adjust the clock to local time?

This will make Fedora use local time (like Windows). The change may cause a temporary jump of a few hours in the clock.

Continue?
ajustes-manutencao.manutencao_fedora_desc: Periodic tasks that keep the system clean and controllable: cache cleanup, kernel management and GRUB settings.
ajustes-manutencao.limpeza_desc: Cleans the DNF cache, orphaned dependencies and unused Flatpak runtimes.
ajustes-manutencao.kernel_desc: Manage the kernels installed on your system.
ajustes-manutencao.kernel_aviso: ⚠️ IMPORTANT: Removing an older kernel version is not recommended — Fedora keeps only the last 3 kernels.
ajustes-manutencao.kernel_msg_atual_nao_removivel:
❌ Cannot remove the kernel you are currently using ({kernel}).

Reboot with another kernel before removing this one.
ajustes-manutencao.kernel_confirmar_remocao:
⚠️ WARNING!

You are about to remove the kernel:
{kernel}

Are you sure you want to continue?
ajustes-manutencao.grub_desc: Configure GRUB to always show when the computer turns on and set the display time to 10 seconds.
ajustes-manutencao.grub_aviso: ⚠️ This change affects system boot. Make sure GRUB is installed correctly.
ajustes-manutencao.grub_confirmar_recomendado:
⚠️ Apply the recommended GRUB configuration?

• GRUB will always show on boot
• Display time: 10 seconds
ajustes-manutencao.grub_confirmar_padrao: Restore default GRUB configuration (timeout=5 seconds, hidden)?

estado-fedora.descricao: Fedora-specific information and tools: installed version check, Fedora Atomic/Silverblue (immutable systems) detection and SELinux management — Fedora's mandatory security system, often poorly understood by those coming from other distributions.
estado-fedora.aviso_geral: ℹ️ This session is informative. Commands here only read system state. Nothing is changed without you explicitly clicking a button — and the ones that do change make clear what they do.
estado-fedora.versao_desc: FAP is developed and tested on Fedora 44. If you're on a different version, some commands may behave unexpectedly (renamed packages, changed repositories, new syntax). This check warns you when that happens.
estado-fedora.versao_info: ℹ️ Supported versions: Fedora 43, 44 and 45. Older versions (42 and earlier) or newer (46+) may require manual adjustments. FAP keeps working, but you may need to adapt a specific command.
estado-fedora.atomic_desc: Fedora has two variants: "traditional" (Workstation, KDE, etc) and "immutable" (Silverblue, Kinoite, Bazzite, Bluefin). On immutable variants, the base system is protected and cannot be modified by dnf install — only by rpm-ostree or bootc.
estado-fedora.atomic_info: ℹ️ Why this matters: FAP uses dnf to install most packages. If you're on an immutable system, those commands will fail (or worse, require override). This detection warns you before you try something that won't work.
estado-fedora.selinux_desc: SELinux is Fedora's mandatory access control system. It enforces strict rules about what each process can do — even processes running as root are limited. It's Fedora's biggest mystery for those coming from other distributions, and the most common cause of "why doesn't this work?".
estado-fedora.selinux_status_desc: Shows the current SELinux mode (enforcing, permissive or disabled).
estado-fedora.selinux_status_info:
ℹ️ SELinux modes:
  • Enforcing — rules active and real blocks. It's Fedora's default and recommended mode.
  • Permissive — rules active but only logs, doesn't block. Good for diagnosing.
  • Disabled — rules deactivated. Not recommended — reduces system security.
estado-fedora.selinux_trouble_desc: Lists "AVC denial" warnings from the last 24 hours. Each AVC is an access attempt that SELinux blocked. Not every block is a problem — many are noise from processes trying to access things outside the policy, but the pattern helps identify real problems.
estado-fedora.selinux_trouble_info: ℹ️ How to interpret: an isolated AVC is usually harmless. Multiple repeated AVCs from the same process indicate it's trying something SELinux doesn't allow — that deserves investigation.
estado-fedora.setroubleshoot_desc: Installs setroubleshoot, an official Fedora package that automatically analyzes each AVC and suggests a fix — in plain language, without SELinux jargon. It's what turns "usuário_u:role_r:tipo_t" into "Apache cannot read files in /var/www/html, you should run such command".
estado-fedora.setroubleshoot_info: ℹ️ What is installed: setroubleshoot-server (analysis engine), setools-console (CLI tools) and policycoreutils-python-utils (policy utilities). Warnings appear automatically in the desktop notification menu when an AVC is generated.
estado-fedora.selinux_gui_desc: Installs policycoreutils-gui, which provides a complete graphical interface to manage SELinux: booleans, file contexts, port mapping, users, and other advanced settings. It's the friendliest way to view and adjust SELinux on Fedora.
estado-fedora.selinux_gui_info:
ℹ️ What you can do with it:
  • View and toggle booleans (feature on/off switches)
  • View file contexts (what each folder can access)
  • Configure allowed ports for each service
  • Manage SELinux users
estado-fedora.selinux_gui_info_root: ℹ️ About the password: when opening the SELinux Manager, it will ask for administrator password — this is normal. Without root, it only allows viewing; to change things, privilege is required.
estado-fedora.selinux_desabilitar_desc: Many tutorials on the internet recommend disabling SELinux when something doesn't work. This is not a good practice on Fedora — the system is designed to work with it enabled, and disabling masks problems instead of solving them.
estado-fedora.selinux_desabilitar_info: ℹ️ If you need to change the mode: the official tool is setenforce. Running sudo setenforce 0 sets it to permissive until the next boot. To make it permanent, edit /etc/selinux/config (we don't do this automatically — it's your decision).

sobre-FAP.sobre_o_que: Fedora Advantage Panel (FAP) is a visual automation panel for setting up Fedora Linux. It brings together, in a friendly interface, the steps that would normally require terminal commands — from the initial system tuning to getting everything ready for daily use and gaming.
sobre-FAP.sobre_porque: Fedora is excellent, but it requires some initial steps (enabling RPM Fusion, installing codecs, configuring drivers) that often intimidate users coming from distributions like Ubuntu, Linux Mint or Zorin OS. FAP automates those steps and presents them clearly, in guided sessions — without you having to remember commands or search for tutorials.
sobre-FAP.sobre_ganhos: With FAP, you get your Fedora complete in a few clicks: multimedia codecs, essential repositories, AMD/NVIDIA drivers, graphics acceleration, gaming support (Steam, Heroic, Lutris, Proton), productivity tools, internet apps, audio and video editing, and much more. All with real-time logs and without needing to open the terminal.
sobre-FAP.sobre_nao_faz_1: It does not replace the terminal — when something goes wrong, some problems still require manual commands for diagnosis.
sobre-FAP.sobre_nao_faz_2: It does not install games — it prepares the system for you to install and run games, but does not download or install games themselves.
sobre-FAP.sobre_nao_faz_3: It does not back up your data — we always recommend having snapshots or a backup before making system changes.
sobre-FAP.sobre_nao_faz_4: It is not affiliated with Red Hat — it is an independent project maintained by the community.
sobre-FAP.sobre_nao_faz_5: It is not an operating system installer — FAP configures an already-installed Fedora, it does not install Fedora from scratch.
